migration.description: Add user ownership and explicit share grants for Host resources, per-user default Host routing, and durable Connector enrollment binding and retry state.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one Host ownership and Connector browser enrollment repair; migration 00018 must be present before this ordered application migration is applied.

compatibility_assessment.reason: The migration adds Host ownership/share administration and binds Connector device authorization to the approving user and optional existing Host. Existing singleton Host rows remain readable as ownerless legacy rows but are denied by user-scoped routing until explicitly reconciled by a future owner-aware action.

durable_state.description: New Host rows identify an owning auth user. Active share grants are explicit and revocable, and a per-user default maps session/run creation to one owned or shared Host. Connector device rows retain the approving user, requested Host and an exchange claim so credential issuance can be retried after an enrollment failure.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL tables and columns managed by the embedded Goose application migration history.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_versions: Phase-one Connector browser-enrollment candidate containing migration 00018.
source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one user-owned Host candidate containing migration 00019.
source_compatibility_range.compatibility_boundary: Older candidates are not a safe rollback target after ownerful Hosts, explicit shares, per-user defaults or device exchange claims are written. The new candidate never falls back to the old global Host selection and does not infer ownership for the preserved legacy singleton row. Legacy state remains readable only before this candidate writes the new ownership state; recovery after cutover is forward-only.

ordered_operations.description: Make the historical singleton marker nullable and add nullable owner_user_id so existing ownerless rows remain readable without constraining new Host rows.
Create host_share_grants and its active-user index for explicit, revocable Host access.
Create host_user_defaults and its reverse index for deterministic per-user session/run routing.
Add requested_host_id and exchange_started_at to device authorizations with an index for claimed, unconsumed exchanges.

database_migration.backfill: none; existing singleton Host rows remain ownerless and are quarantined from user-scoped routing rather than assigned to an arbitrary user.
rollout_signals: Goose records migration 00019 only after all additive tables, columns and indexes commit in order.
Host enrollment writes owner_user_id and a user default in one transaction, while explicit grants are checked against the Host owner under a row lock.
Session and run routing resolves only host_user_defaults joined to current ownership or an active share; no query orders all Host rows as a fallback.
Connector exchange claims an authorized row before enrollment and clears the claim on enrollment failure; consumed_at is written only after a credential is durably created.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version; switchback to an older candidate is unsupported after the additive ownership state is written; ownerless legacy rows are not auto-assigned during recovery

validation: Migration inspection confirms nullable legacy singleton compatibility, owner/share/default foreign keys, active-share indexing and exchange claim indexing.
Owner-only credential and share administration rejects foreign identities, while an active explicit share permits host use and revocation removes that access.
User-scoped Host lookup returns no Host when the user has no default or only an ownerless legacy row, even when another user owns a Host.

Concurrent device exchange attempts permit one final enrollment side effect, failed enrollment releases the claim, and a consumed authorization can replay the idempotent enrollment while its bounded authorization lifetime remains valid.
